Following an example from a team, where we have 20+ outliers, and comparison with the CT PBC (way less).

facts.F342: Where the rule lives: the outlier rule moves to the backend, Flow metrics module, behind a replaceable definition. Interface ICycleTimeOutlierDefinition (Modules/FlowMetrics/Application/CycleTimeOutlierDefinition.cs) has one method: OutlierVerdict Judge(IReadOnlyList<int> baselineCycleTimes, IReadOnlyList<CycleTimeObservation> shown). It lives in Application, not Domain, because the Architecture.FlowMetrics rule lets only its listed types reach the module Domain and that list only shrinks. The only implementation now is UpperNaturalProcessLimitOutlierDefinition, in the same file, registered once as a singleton in Program.cs next to the metrics services and injected by constructor into TeamMetricsService and PortfolioMetricsService. A later definition is supplied by registering another implementation; the route, the DTO, the services and the frontend do not change. The frontend keeps no rule: it partitions the plotted items by the outlier ids of the verdict. Confirms the DISCUSS proposals: limit = the Cycle Time PBC UNPL (average + 2.66 x average moving range of the baseline Cycle Times, configured baseline or else the selected range), compared unrounded; only above-UNPL sets an item apart; no silent 5 x median fallback.
facts.F343: Carriers and owners. Domain (Modules/FlowMetrics/Domain): UpperNaturalProcessLimit value object in XmRCalculator.cs, holding the unrounded double, built by XmRCalculator.UpperNaturalProcessLimitOf(int[] baseline) and answering IsExceededBy(int days) as days > limit; XmRCalculator.Calculate and its large-change rule use the same object, so the PBC marker and the outlier rule share one formula and one comparison. Application (Modules/FlowMetrics/Application/CycleTimeOutlierDefinition.cs): OutlierVerdict closed choice (abstract record with two cases): Limited(UpperNaturalProcessLimit Limit, IReadOnlyList<int> OutlierWorkItemIds), which exposes UpperNaturalProcessLimitDays so the DTO never touches the Domain type, and NoLimits; CycleTimeObservation(int WorkItemId, int Days) record; ICycleTimeOutlierDefinition and UpperNaturalProcessLimitOutlierDefinition. Application services: GetCycleTimeOutliers(owner, startDate, endDate, int? definitionId) on ITeamMetricsService and IPortfolioMetricsService, built once in BaseMetricsService.BuildCycleTimeOutliers: it resolves the baseline with ResolveBaseline, collects baseline and shown Cycle Times with the same window, filter (Cycle Time > 0) and order as BuildCycleTimeProcessBehaviourChart (a named definition uses each item named duration, items without one are skipped), and asks the injected definition; cached through GetFromCacheIfExists with a key that includes the definition id. API: GET cycleTime/outliers?startDate&endDate&definitionId on TeamMetricsController and PortfolioMetricsController, next to cycleTime/pbc, under the same RbacGuard read requirement; DTO CycleTimeOutliersDto (API/DTO) with Status (CycleTimeOutlierStatus Ready or NoLimits, serialised as a string), UpperNaturalProcessLimit (double or null, read from UpperNaturalProcessLimitDays) and OutlierWorkItemIds (int array). Frontend: ICycleTimeOutliers model (models/Metrics/CycleTimeOutliers.ts), MetricsService.getCycleTimeOutliers for Team and Portfolio, a keyed TanStack query in the chart, owner and range passed to the chart through widgetNodes and BaseMetricsView, and a verdict-pending state of the outlier header chip while the verdict loads. Per-process state: none new beyond the existing metrics cache; the switch is React component state only.

facts.F61: Loading and failure looks: the verdict is a keyed TanStack query owned by the chart, key [ownerKind, ownerId, startDate, endDate, definitionId or default], fetched whenever the scatterplot is shown, independent of the PBC widget. While it is pending or failed no item is set apart and no count is shown: pending reuses the chip loading wording (Outliers / Outliers, loading, disabled) and the chart reports loading up to its WidgetShell frame through the existing widget status channel, so the frame dims under its spinner; a failed query reports failure so the frame shows its could-not-load look. A late answer for an older key never lands (the key differs; no placeholder data from another key). Confirms the DISCUSS proposal.
facts.F62: No usable limits: the verdict is NoLimits when the resolved baseline is invalid (missing, or shorter than 14 days) or holds fewer than 2 positive Cycle Times (the PBC then draws UNPL = the single value or 0 and marks nothing). The chart then sets no item apart, draws every item with the pre-outlier axis, shows no count chip and shows in the chip place the text: No outliers: the {Cycle Time} process behaviour chart has no limits for this date range. The info popover says outliers need those limits. Never a fallback to 5 x median. Confirms the DISCUSS proposal.
facts.F63: Wording (Terminology words): help sentence An outlier is a closed {Work Item} whose {Cycle Time} is above the upper natural process limit of the {Cycle Time} process behaviour chart for this date range. List title {Work Items} with a {Cycle Time} above the upper natural process limit ({N} days), where N is the unrounded limit shown with at most one decimal (30.6, 30), so the stated limit and the listed set never disagree. Confirms the DISCUSS proposal with that precision.
facts.F64: Formal verification: the claims are pure, finite, request-response functions with no concurrency, waiting or recovery (one verdict per request). Claim-to-checker: outlier membership and NoLimits laws -> executable example tables at the application-service port plus a fast-check property on the frontend partition; no Quint/TLA+/Agda model was authored or run because the root context for this feature directed no formal model checking and a short algebraic note; the formal-proof axis of these claims is INDETERMINATE (not executed), never PASS. Liveness is not applicable: no state machine, no retry and no waiting; each request is a finite computation over a bounded list.

An unknown or invalid named definition yields NoLimits; the chart already resets such a selection to the default.
